title: The hotel
_about: A story-and-a-half dogtrot. The public side is the 'ordinary' — a fire, one long common table, and a dram bar. The other side is the sleeping room: four beds, and you do not get one to yourself. Travellers are how news reaches Gonzales, so this is the room where a student finds out what is happening somewhere else.
_honesty: Sources disagree about whose hotel this was. The 1836 building list says Turner's Hotel; George Davis's biography says he kept 'the only hotel in Gonzales.' Show students both and let them weigh a list against a life-sketch — that is a better history lesson than either answer. The long table laid with mismatched knives, everything from butcher knives to pocketknives, and gourd cups instead of glass, is from an eyewitness.

landmarks.label: THE BREEZEWAY
landmarks.note: Open at both ends, like every house in this town.

landmarks.label: THE LONG TABLE
landmarks.note: Mismatched knives — butcher knives to pocketknives — and gourd cups. Everyone eats together or nobody eats.

landmarks.label: THE DRAM BAR
landmarks.note: A whiskey barrel and a tin cup on a string.

landmarks.label: THE LADDER
landmarks.note: Up to the half-storey, where more travellers sleep. And where their bags are.

features.label: A stranger's saddlebags
features.note: Left at the foot of the ladder. Letters, and a newspaper from San Felipe.
